info.title: Kantel API
info.description: Kantel's public API for host apps, such as Lleverage, and for Kantel's own console, which uses it like any other client.

post.description: Starts a session of an agent profile in a project, and sends it `message` when there is one. Needs the operator role on the project. If the first message is refused, the session is closed and the refusal answered.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: The sessions the caller may see, newest first, a page at a time.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where a session works: `project` (in `projectId`) or `organisation`, above every project and in none of them.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: Sessions running in this workspace: the conversations that share its files, each with its own history.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Sessions with every one of these labels, each sent as `label.<key>=<value>`, such as `label.ticket=PROJ-12`.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).
The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Ends the session for good: its sandbox leases, browser sessions and grants end. Closing a closed session does nothing.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Interrupts the session's run in progress, and its child sessions' runs. The conversation keeps its history, and files the run changed stay changed; what the run held ends (its browsers, sandbox leases and grants). The run's result is `aborted`. The session stays open and takes new messages.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.summary: Fork a session from an answer
post.description: Starts a new session in the same project, with the same agent profile and workspace, whose history is this session's up to and including the answer `itemId` names: a second conversation that carries the first one's context and goes its own way. It starts idle. The source session is unchanged. Needs operator on the project; an item that is not an answer in the session's transcript is `not_found`.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Sends the session's agent a message, `via` a prompt, a steer or a follow-up, optionally changing the session's `thinking` level from that run on. Only the session's first message may choose its `model`: once the session has started its model is fixed, and a message naming another is a `conflict`. The answer arrives on the session's stream, and `getRunResult` says when its run has ended. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry can't send it twice: a retry with the same key answers the first call's submission without sending anything, and one with another `via` is a `conflict`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.summary: Wait for a message's run to end
get.description: How the run that a message started or joined ended: `answered` with its final answer, `failed` or `aborted`. Waits up to `timeoutMs` for it and answers 202 `pending` while it goes on, so a host that holds no stream polls this until it ends. A steer's result is the run that acted on it: the run in progress when the steer reached its next model call, or, when it arrived as that run gave its final answer, the run it started straight after on the same conversation. Needs viewer on the session.

parameters.name: submission
parameters.description: The submission's ID, as `sendMessage` answered it. It holds a `/`, so it goes in the query.

parameters.name: timeoutMs
parameters.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds, for the run to end before answering 202 (`pending`). Default 25 s, cut to the server's most (120 s).

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.summary: List the models a session may switch to
get.description: For a model and thinking picker: the models a message's `model` may name, what the session runs with now and what its agent profile names. Naming another model on a message switches the session from that run on (a steer's from the run's next model call) and keeps the conversation's context. Needs viewer on the session.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.summary: List the models a new session could use
get.description: What `getSessionModels` would answer for a session of this agent profile in `projectId`, before it exists, so a New session screen can offer the choice; the first message carries it. `selected` is `defaults`. Needs operator on the project, as creating the session does; `scope=organisation` with no `projectId` answers for a new organisation session, and needs operator across the organisation.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The project the session would run in. Required unless `scope` is `organisation`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where a session works: `project` (in `projectId`) or `organisation`, above every project and in none of them.

200.description: The models a new session would list.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: A hint that a message is coming, such as when someone starts typing: the session's sandbox gets ready for its next command, so it waits for no start. Its container starts only if the session has used one. Idempotent and cheap to repeat; send it at most every few seconds. Needs the operator role on the session.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: The session as `@kantel/protocol` frames: `hello`, then a `snapshot` of its state and latest items (or, with `after`, the deltas after that cursor when the stream still holds them), then a `delta` for every change, live. Fold them with the protocol's `applyFrames`. Over a WebSocket, compressed where the platform can, or as server-sent events.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume after this cursor (a snapshot's or a delta's): the stream sends the deltas after it, or a snapshot when it no longer holds them.

101.description: Upgraded to a WebSocket (send `Upgrade: websocket`). Each message is a JSON array of frames; an empty array is a keep-alive. The server negotiates `permessage-deflate` where the platform can. The client sends nothing; to resume, reconnect with `?after=` and the last cursor it holds.

200.description: The stream. Without an upgrade: server-sent events, each named after its frame's type with the frame as its JSON data, then one `ready` event once the client has caught up. Snapshot and delta events carry their cursor as the event ID, so `Last-Event-ID` resumes too.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: The session's transcript in pages, newest first, for scrolling back past a snapshot's items: start with `before` set to the snapshot's `items[0].id`, then follow `nextCursor`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Items older than this item ID, such as a snapshot's `items[0].id`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many items. Default 50, cut to 200.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.summary: Read an image in a session's transcript
get.description: The bytes of an image a tool item names by reference (`images[].url`), such as a screenshot or a generated image: snapshots, deltas and history pages carry the reference, not the image. `imageId` is the SHA-256 of the image's bytes in lowercase hex, so the same URL always answers the same bytes, and the answer may be cached for good (`cache-control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`). The model still reads the image itself. Needs viewer on the session; an ID the session's transcript doesn't name is `not_found`.

parameters.name: imageId
parameters.description: The SHA-256 of the image's bytes, in lowercase hex.

200.description: The image, as its own type.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: The organisation's schedules the caller may see, a page at a time. A project's schedules are listed only to those with the viewer role on it.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What runs. A `task` starts a session with its payload `{ "agentId"?, "prompt" }` and sends the prompt exactly as written; a `check` runs its payload (a command line or an argument list) with no model.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Exactly one of `at` (a one-off) and `repeat`. A task's runs each start a session, in the schedule's project (the default project for one owned by the organisation or a user), running the payload's agent with its prompt sent exactly as written. Agents may not create schedules. Needs the operator role on a project-owned schedule's project.

post.description: A link for an iframe: a watch-only live view of one of the session's open browsers, or a replay of one, open or closed. Needs viewer on the session; never an agent. The link carries a short-lived token scoped to that one view (never control), lasting `minutes`. A closed browser has no live view (`expired`); a deployment whose browsers keep no recordings has no replay (`unavailable`), and a recording past its retention is `expired`. Audited as `browser.session.embedded`, without the link.

parameters.name: browserSessionId
parameters.description: The browser session's ID, as the session's browser tool items name it.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

Needs operator on the workspace's project, as a person (never an agent or an API key). Audited as `workspace.share.created`, without the token.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).
The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Starts connecting a template or a remote MCP server for an owner (an organisation, a project or a person). Answers a pending attempt with a `connectUrl` on this deployment that expires after 15 minutes and works once; the person it is for opens it and signs in at the provider. An open server is connected at once (`completed`). `refused` with `no_client` when the template needs an OAuth app nobody has registered. Creating needs admin on the owner, or being the person for their own.

mcpUrl.description: A remote MCP server's endpoint, for a server with no template.

scopeSets.description: Scope sets to ask for; default the template's default sets.

scopes.description: Explicit scopes, added to the sets'.

forUserId.description: A handover link: the person who must complete it. Default the caller.

templateId.description: A template with a key auth type. Give this or `custom`.

hosts.description: https hosts the key may be sent to.

value.description: The key. Write-only: never returned. For `basic` injection, `username:password` (split at the first colon; no colon: the user name with an empty password).

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: Which connection a session used, at which step, acting for whom, and who could see the session then; filtered by connection or session, newest first. A use in a private session is listed whole only to the connection's owner, the person the session acted for and whoever may open the session now. Anyone else, an organisation or project admin included, gets it as a `RedactedConnectionUse`: when, how it ended and for whom, with no session, step or request. Naming the session is `forbidden` to them.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

Needs viewer on the session; another person's connection that doesn't reach it shows no account.

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Answer as if the session had this visibility. Default its own.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

clientSecret.description: Write-only. A public client has none.

post.summary: Have GitHub create a GitHub App
post.description: Starts GitHub's app manifest flow: answers `url`, a page on this deployment that posts a manifest for a GitHub App to GitHub (on the person's account, or `githubOrganisation`'s). Once the person chooses Create there, GitHub sends them back and Kantel stores the app's client as an OAuth client for the `github` template at `owner`'s tier, its secret write-only. A person only, with the same rights as registering that client by hand. The flow must finish within an hour; `url` holds its single-use state and is only in this answer.

owner.description: Whose client the app becomes: the caller's organisation, a project (`projectId`) or the caller.

githubOrganisation.description: The GitHub organisation to create it in; the person's own GitHub account when absent.

returnTo.description: Where GitHub's redirect back ends up: a path on this deployment, or an https URL.

201.description: The flow, with the page to open.

get.description: Where it has got to: pending, created (with the OAuth client and the app), failed or expired.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

delete.description: Stops every use at once, asks the provider to revoke its tokens where the provider can (RFC 7009, or the provider's own endpoint), destroys the stored credential, and removes the connection with its rules and any approvals not yet used. A revoke the provider refuses still removes it: `revocation` says what happened upstream, and the `connections.connection.removed` audit event records the same. Its uses and audit history stay.

200.description: Removed, and what happened at the provider.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

value.description: The new key. Write-only: never returned.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.summary: Share a person's connection with a project
post.description: Only its owner, as a person, into a project where they hold operator. Every attended session in the project may then use it, whoever it acts for and whoever can see it; its rules still decide each request, and unattended sessions never get it. Sharing again changes nothing. Audited as `connections.connection.shared` (#335).

projectId.description: The project to share it with.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

delete.summary: Stop sharing a connection with a project
delete.description: Its owner, or an admin of the project. The project's next request through it is refused and recorded as denied. Audited as `connections.connection.unshared` (#335).

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The project it is shared with.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: Asks the provider, through the connection, what it can reach now (#461). For GitHub: the installations of the app the person can reach (`GET /user/installations`) and each one's repositories, at most 300, with `truncated` when there are more. Only someone who manages the connection (admin on its owner, or the person for their own); never an agent. `not_supported` for a provider Kantel can't ask. Never answers a secret.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

get.description: Who may use it for what, and on what terms (`allow`, `ask` or `deny`), with what a request no rule matches gets (`unmatched`) and the rules' version. A connection made before rules is given its template's defaults (reads allow, writes ask, deletes deny, `unmatched` ask) the first time its rules are read, and `defaults` says when. Needs viewer on the connection's owner.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

patch.summary: Change what unmatched requests get, or reset the defaults

sessionId.description: The session the request came from.

Account.title: Account
Account.description: An account the caller may act in, with the caller's role in it.

AccountKind.title: AccountKind
AccountKind.description: `personal`: one person's own account, made at their first sign-in; what they create is theirs alone unless they move it. `organisation`: an account people create or join, where sandboxes and snapshots are shared.

AccountLimits.title: AccountLimits
AccountLimits.description: The account's limits, where the deployment sets any.

Actor.title: Actor
Actor.description: Who acted: a person, a host app's API key, an agent or Kantel itself.

prefix.description: The secret's first characters, such as `ksk_5n2p`, to tell keys apart.

sandboxIds.description: Limited to these sandboxes (and the ones it creates).

ApiKey.title: ApiKey
ApiKey.description: A scoped API key. Its secret is never stored or shown after it is made.

ApiKeyPreset.title: ApiKeyPreset
ApiKeyPreset.description: A named set of scopes. `read-only`: the `:read` scopes. `agent`: what a coding agent needs to make and drive its own sandboxes, everything but `sandboxes:delete` and the account and host scopes. `ci`: `agent` plus `sandboxes:delete`. `admin`: every scope but `hosts:admin`.

ApiKeyScope.title: ApiKeyScope
ApiKeyScope.description: What a key may do. `sandboxes:read`: list and inspect sandboxes, their usage and events. `sandboxes:write`: create, change, start, stop, pause, resume, fork and recover. `sandboxes:delete`: delete for good. `exec`: run commands. `files`: read and write files. `access`: SSH, desktop, browser and public ports. `snapshots:read`, `snapshots:write`: snapshots and saved snapshots. `account:read`: the account, its members and keys. `account:admin`: members, keys, webhooks, telemetry and the proxy. `hosts:admin`: the deployment's hosts, for a super-admin's key only.

streaming.description: True while tokens are still arriving.

Attention.title: Attention
Attention.description: How a session list groups the session: working, waiting on someone, or done.

url.description: Watch and drive the sandbox's Chrome in a browser.

cdpUrl.description: A Chrome DevTools Protocol WebSocket URL, for Playwright's `connectOverCDP` or Puppeteer.

url.description: The page to frame. It holds its token after `#`, so the token reaches no server; treat the URL as a secret.

endMessage.description: What the page posts to its parent once its stream is over.

callId.description: The `browser_request` call waiting on a person: for a code mode script's request, its inner call (`<scriptCallId>/<key>`). A person answers it with `POST /browser/decisions`.

sites.description: The sites the agent asked for.

BrowserGrantCard.title: BrowserGrantCard
BrowserGrantCard.description: An agent's request for a browser that a code mode script made: the transcript carries it while the call waits, and settles it when the call returns (`denied` also when no one answered).

accountId.description: The account the call acts in when it names none.

superAdmin.description: Whether the caller may manage the deployment's hosts.

Caller.title: Caller
Caller.description: Who is calling, the accounts they may act in, and the deployment's mode.

CallerApiKey.title: CallerApiKey
CallerApiKey.description: The key the call was signed in with, when it was a key.

setup.description: `ready`: the caller can connect now. `needs_client`: it needs an OAuth app someone must register first.

signIn.description: For a ready OAuth connect: in a browser window, or by typing a code at the provider.

reraiseHours.description: Hours before a finding still present is raised again. Default 6.

risingFactor.description: A finding whose value grows by this factor is raised again. Default 2.

failuresBeforeRaise.description: Failed runs in a row before a `check-failed` finding is raised. Default 3.

severityOrder.description: Severities, worst first, case-insensitive, for raising a finding that got worse as `escalated`. Default `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `warn`, `info`.

ClientRegistration.title: ClientRegistration
ClientRegistration.description: How Kantel gets an OAuth client: a pre-registered `client`, the deployment's client ID metadata document (`cimd`), or dynamic registration (`dcr`).

stdout.description: Its output so far, up to 1 MiB; `truncated` says if there was more.

sources.description: What backs it: URLs, `owner/repo@commit:path:lines`, ticket IDs.

staleAfter.description: After this, recall marks it stale (epoch milliseconds).

extensions.description: Namespaced host data Kantel keeps but doesn't read, such as Lleverage's `lleverage.workflows`.

setBy.description: `owner`: set by the space's owner. `learned`: from an approved agent proposal.

ConceptScope.title: ConceptScope
ConceptScope.description: Where a concept applies. A `job` concept is an exception for one job.

connectUrl.description: Open this to sign in. Present while pending; it expires and works once.

userCode.description: The code the person types at `verificationUri`.

interval.description: Seconds between asking after the attempt.

device.description: A sign-in with a code (the OAuth device flow), while pending. Each read of the attempt asks the provider, at most once per interval.

hosts.description: Hosts the credential may be sent to.

placeholder.description: What a sandbox sends where the credential goes (#331). Not a secret: the egress gate swaps it for the credential, only for a session that may use the connection, only to one of its hosts.

shares.description: For a person's connection: the projects its owner shared it with (#335). Any attended session there may use it.

Connection.title: Connection
Connection.description: One authorisation against a provider or remote MCP server. No secret.

callId.description: The tool call waiting on this approval: a connection call's `callId`, or for a request a `codemode` script made, the script's inner call (`<scriptCallId>/<key>`, such as `toolu_01/c9`). A client that renders that call may show the approval in it and leave this card out; one that doesn't still has the card. Absent on cards written before it.

ConnectionApprovalCard.title: ConnectionApprovalCard
ConnectionApprovalCard.description: A connection request waiting on a person: a credential an agent asked to use. The secret is never part of it.

url.description: The URL as it will be sent, query included.

tool.description: For an MCP tool call: the tool.

digest.description: The exact request's digest: only an identical request matches it.

ConnectionApprovalRequest.title: ConnectionApprovalRequest
ConnectionApprovalRequest.description: For an approval of one exact request a rule asked about (#333). Its headers and body are on the connection request page.

callId.description: The tool call: a connection tool's own `callId`, or a script's inner call (`toolu_01/c9`). `/v1/connections/uses` records it as `toolCallId`.

templateId.description: The catalogue template it was made from, such as `github`.

account.description: Whose identity acted, in the service's words: a login, a name or an email.

viaShare.description: A person's connection used in a project it is shared with.

query.description: The query as sent, without its `?`.

tool.description: For an MCP call: the tool.

operation.description: What it did, when the connection's template classifies it.

reason.description: Why it was refused or held.

ConnectionCallDetails.title: ConnectionCallDetails
ConnectionCallDetails.description: Which connection a call used, as whose account, what it did, what decided it and how the service answered. Never a credential.

set.description: `false`: the organisation has no ceiling, and nothing is bounded.

ConnectionCeiling.title: ConnectionCeiling
ConnectionCeiling.description: The organisation's ceiling: no rule may allow or ask outside it.

ConnectionClientRef.title: ConnectionClientRef
ConnectionClientRef.description: The OAuth client a connection is pinned to.

ConnectionDecision.title: ConnectionDecision
ConnectionDecision.description: What the proxy does with one request, and why.

state.description: `ok`: the last refresh worked. `refresh_failing`: the last refresh failed in a way that may pass (no answer, a 5xx, a rate limit); the connection stays active and Kantel retries with backoff. `needs_reconnect`: the provider refused the refresh token; requests are refused with `connection_reconnect_required` until a person connects it again.

reason.description: The last failure, in plain words. Never a secret.

failures.description: Refreshes that failed in a row.

retryAt.description: When Kantel tries again. Epoch milliseconds, UTC.

refreshedAt.description: When a refresh last worked. Epoch milliseconds, UTC.

ConnectionHealth.title: ConnectionHealth
ConnectionHealth.description: A connection's health, which Kantel sets from its token refreshes (#328), apart from its status.

ConnectionKind.title: ConnectionKind
ConnectionKind.description: `mcp`: a remote MCP server the agent calls tools on. `http`: an HTTP API.

id.description: The template's own name for it, such as `issues/create-comment`.

group.description: The template's permission group: GitHub's `profile`, `repo` or `workflow`.

resource.description: The one repository it acts on, `owner/name`, when the request names exactly one.

ConnectionOperation.title: ConnectionOperation
ConnectionOperation.description: What a request did, as its connection's template classifies it.

ConnectionOwner.title: ConnectionOwner
ConnectionOwner.description: Who owns a connection: an organisation, a project or a person.

total.description: How many repositories GitHub counts in all, listed or not.

truncated.description: GitHub has more than were listed (at most 300).

manageUrl.description: Where to choose the repositories on GitHub.

ConnectionReach.title: ConnectionReach
ConnectionReach.description: What a connection can reach at its provider (#461), read through it now: for GitHub, the app's installations and their repositories. Never a secret.

repositorySelection.description: `all`: every repository the account has. `selected`: only those chosen at install.

manageUrl.description: The installation's settings page on GitHub.

ConnectionReachInstallation.title: ConnectionReachInstallation
ConnectionReachInstallation.description: One installation of the GitHub App the person can reach.

rulesRemoved.description: Standing access rules removed with it.

approvalsWithdrawn.description: Approvals of exact requests not yet used, withdrawn or stopped with it.

ConnectionRemoval.title: ConnectionRemoval
ConnectionRemoval.description: What a disconnect did, in Kantel and at the provider.

endpoint.description: The endpoint Kantel called. Never carries a token.

reason.description: Why it is `unsupported` or `failed`, in plain words.

manageUrl.description: The provider's page for removing an app's access.

maxUses.description: It stops matching once `uses` reaches this.

source.description: The template's defaults, a person, an approval's "always allow", or a migrated vault policy.

approvalId.description: The approval whose "always allow" saved it.

ConnectionRule.title: ConnectionRule
ConnectionRule.description: One access rule on a connection.

ConnectionRuleAction.title: ConnectionRuleAction
ConnectionRuleAction.description: What a rule answers. `ask` goes to an approval (#333).

version.description: Goes up on every change to the rules, not on a use. Part of an approval's digest (#333).

defaults.description: The last time Kantel set these rules to the template's defaults, and why.

ConnectionRules.title: ConnectionRules
ConnectionRules.description: A connection's rules, and what a request no rule matches gets (`unmatched`).

path.description: A path pattern of whole segments: `*` is one segment, a trailing `/**` any rest.

host.description: One of the connection's hosts. Default any of them.

group.description: The template's permission group, such as GitHub's `profile`, `repo` or `workflow`.

resource.description: A repository, `owner/name`, or `owner/*` for every one of an owner's. Case is ignored.

ConnectionRuleWhat.title: ConnectionRuleWhat
ConnectionRuleWhat.description: What a rule covers: any request, an API endpoint by method and path pattern, one MCP tool, or requests the template classifies (`operation`) by permission group, access and repository; each it names must match.

ConnectionRuleWho.title: ConnectionRuleWho
ConnectionRuleWho.description: Who a rule is for: any agent, sessions a person is present for (`attended`), scheduled runs and other sessions with no person present (`unattended`), organisation-level agents (sessions in no project), a project, an agent profile or one session.

projectId.description: The project it is shared with.

ConnectionShare.title: ConnectionShare
ConnectionShare.description: A person's connection shared with a project (#335): explicit, audited and revocable.

personal.description: Every session acting for a person is that person's alone (a deployment with one person), so their personal connections work in all their sessions. False: a session is seen by its project, and a person's connection is refused in it unless they share it with the project.

ConnectionsSettings.title: ConnectionsSettings
ConnectionsSettings.description: How this deployment runs connections. No secrets.

projects.description: Only sessions in these projects (an organisation's connection).

actingUsers.description: Only sessions acting for these people.

agents.description: Only sessions of these agent profiles.

visibility.description: `private`: only in sessions nobody but the acting person can see.

ConnectionUsage.title: ConnectionUsage
ConnectionUsage.description: Where a connection may be used, by whom and in which sessions.

toolCallId.description: The tool call (step) that used it.

account.description: Whose identity acted: the connection's account in the service's words (a login, name or email).

viaShare.description: A person's connection used in a project it is shared with, not by its owner's own session.

egress.description: Sent by the sandbox through the egress gate with the connection's placeholder (#331).

decision.description: What the access rules answered, when the request got as far as them.

ConnectionUse.title: ConnectionUse
ConnectionUse.description: Which connection a session used, at which step, and who could see it.

ratePerHour.description: What an hour of running costs at its size, in `currency`.

Cost.description: What a sandbox costs at the deployment's rates. A self-hosted install's rates are 0 unless its operator sets them.

CreateApiKeyBody.description: Give `scopes` or a `preset` (or both, which adds them). A key can't hold a scope its maker lacks.

agentId.description: The agent profile the session runs.

pinnedAt.description: When the session was pinned to the top of the list, in epoch milliseconds.

archivedAt.description: When the session was archived (out of the default list), in epoch milliseconds.

markedUnreadAt.description: When someone marked the session unread, in epoch milliseconds.

CreatedSession.title: CreatedSession
CreatedSession.description: A new session, with its first message's submission when it was sent one.

CreatedToolServer.title: CreatedToolServer
CreatedToolServer.description: A new server, and for a tunnel its first token.

email.description: Only this person may use it. Absent: anyone with the code.

name.description: The project's name, trimmed: not empty, and at most 100 characters.

CreateProjectBody.description: Any other field is refused as `invalid`.

parentShareId.description: Required of an agent: the share it passes on.

image.description: A microVM's base image. Default: the deployment's.

from.description: Start from this snapshot: a snapshot's ID or a saved snapshot's name in the account.

env.description: Environment variables every command sees. Not secrets: they are shown to anyone who may exec.

hostLabels.description: Place it only on a host with each label, such as `{ site: "home" }`.

wait.description: Answer once it is `running` (or `error`) rather than as soon as it is placed.

CreateSandboxBody.title: CreateSandboxBody
CreateSandboxBody.description: Every field is optional: `{}` makes a running isolate in the caller's account.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as `Europe/London`.

at.description: A one-off at this instant (epoch milliseconds). Exactly one of `at` and `repeat`.

until.description: No occurrence is due after this (epoch milliseconds).

CreateScheduleBody.description: A new schedule. Needs the operator role on a project-owned schedule's project.

userId.description: The person the session works for. A person may name only themselves; a host app any user. Default the person creating it.

workspaceId.description: An existing workspace to run in.

parentSessionId.description: Creates a child session owned by this parent; aborting the parent aborts it.

CreateSessionBody.description: Put the host's own reference for the session in `labels`, such as `{ lleverageRunId: "run-42" }`, and find it again with `GET /sessions?label.lleverageRunId=run-42`.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

last4.description: A key's or client secret's last four characters.

CredentialState.title: CredentialState
CredentialState.description: A credential's state. Never its value.

Cursor.title: Cursor
Cursor.description: An opaque position in a session's stream.

agentWrites.description: Let agents write through the share the grant makes (default false). Only when it grants `edit` or `approve`.

revision.description: Pins this revision. Without one, the share follows the latest.

DecideAccessRequestBody.title: DecideAccessRequestBody
DecideAccessRequestBody.description: A grant may narrow what was asked (a weaker permission, an earlier expiry, a pinned revision), never widen it.

path.description: Keys and indexes to a string in the tool item's `args`; missing ones are created.

DeltaOp.title: DeltaOp
DeltaOp.description: `append` adds an item, `replace` swaps the item with the same id, `text` appends streamed text to an assistant item, `args` appends streamed text to a string in a tool item's arguments, and `status`, `title` and `usage` set the session's.

DeploymentMode.title: DeploymentMode
DeploymentMode.description: `selfhosted`: an install someone runs for themselves. `hosted`: a hosted service with plans.

url.description: Opens the desktop in a browser. Anyone holding it may use it until it expires.

DraftDocument.title: DraftDocument
DraftDocument.description: The document the model is writing in a `create_document` call, while the answer streams. Gone once the answer is done.

message.description: Why, in a sentence. Never carries a secret.

EgressRefusal.title: EgressRefusal
EgressRefusal.description: The JSON body of the 403 the egress gate answers a sandbox's outbound request with when it refuses it (#331). `approval_pending` adds the approval to wait on.

EgressRefusalCode.title: EgressRefusalCode
EgressRefusalCode.description: Why the egress gate refused a sandbox's request (#331): `host_not_bound` (the placeholder's connection is not for that host), `raw_secret` (a stored secret's own value, not its placeholder), `unknown_placeholder`, `ambiguous_placeholder`, `connection_not_usable`, `needs_reauth`, `https_required`, `rule_denied`, `approval_pending`, `egress_denied` or `egress_unavailable`.

mode.description: `live`: the open browser as it is now, watch-only. `replay`: its recording.

minutes.description: How long the link lasts. Default 15.

path.description: `*` matches one segment; a trailing `/**` the rest.

placeholders.description: Whether connection placeholders work on it, through Kantel's proxy.

Environment.title: Environment
Environment.description: A long-lived machine owned by a project, by default by one person in it, that sessions attach to.

template.description: A provider template, such as a boat saved snapshot.

repository.description: A repository to keep a warm clone of: `owner/name`.

setup.description: Run once after the machine is first created.

EnvironmentDefinition.title: EnvironmentDefinition
EnvironmentDefinition.description: What a fresh machine starts with.

EnvironmentDetail.title: EnvironmentDetail
EnvironmentDetail.description: An environment with the sessions holding it and its recent history.

EnvironmentEgress.title: EnvironmentEgress
EnvironmentEgress.description: `unmanaged`: Kantel doesn't run the machine's network, and code on it reaches the internet directly.

EnvironmentGrant.title: EnvironmentGrant
EnvironmentGrant.description: A session's permission to use an environment, by its alias.

worktree.description: The session's own directory on the machine.

portBase.description: The first of the session's ten ports.

EnvironmentLease.title: EnvironmentLease
EnvironmentLease.description: A session's hold on a running environment.

userId.description: Absent: every member's sessions in the project may attach.

EnvironmentProviderKind.title: EnvironmentProviderKind
EnvironmentProviderKind.description: Who provides the machine. Only `boat` and `fake` are built yet.

lastMs.description: The last start, from the start call to the machine up, in milliseconds.

p50Ms.description: The median of the recent starts.

EnvironmentState.title: EnvironmentState
EnvironmentState.description: `running`: up with at least one session's lease. `idle`: up with none, stopping at `idleStopAt`. `stopped`: no machine running; the disk is kept. `error`: the last operation failed, and Start tries again.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: Every error: the KantelError's code and message.

id.description: The event's ID, such as `evt_8x7w6v`: a webhook's delivery ID, so deduplicate on it.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: Something that happened in an account: what webhooks deliver and the history shows.

EventType.title: EventType
EventType.description: `sandbox.created`: made, before it runs. `sandbox.running`: it runs commands now, after a create, resume, fork or recovery. `sandbox.stopped`, `sandbox.paused`: it stopped (by a call or its auto-stop), or paused. `sandbox.error`: it entered `error`. `sandbox.degraded`, `sandbox.recovered`: its host lost and regained it. `sandbox.deleted`: erased. `snapshot.saved`, `snapshot.deleted`: a saved snapshot was made or deleted.

url.description: Its HTTPS URL. Unless `public`, it carries a token anyone holding it may use.

public.description: Anyone with the URL may open it, with no token. Default false.

FileContent.title: FileContent
FileContent.description: A file of at most 1 MiB; for larger, run a command or use SSH.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the file is in.

path.description: The file's path in the workspace.

title.description: What the link's page calls the file.

token.description: The link's secret: the link is `/shared/<token>` on the deployment's hostname. Treat it as one.

createdBy.description: The person who shared the file, its owner.

text.description: The message's words. May be empty when `attachments` has a file; otherwise it is `invalid`.

attachments.description: Files for this message, in the order they were attached. A deployment that stores no uploads refuses them (`invalid`), as it does a file from another project.

model.description: A model ID the session may use, for this run and the session's later runs. Absent keeps the session's model. Only a session's first message may choose its model: once the session has started, naming another is a `conflict` (naming its own is fine).

FirstMessage.title: FirstMessage
FirstMessage.description: The session's first prompt, sent as soon as it exists.

snapshotId.description: Fork from this snapshot of the sandbox. Default: its newest, or its live state.

itemId.description: The transcript item ID of an assistant answer, as the session's stream gives it.

title.description: The new session's title. Default the source's, with " (fork)".

ForkSessionBody.title: ForkSessionBody
ForkSessionBody.description: Where to fork: the answer the new session's history ends with.

htmlUrl.description: The app's settings page on GitHub.

installUrl.description: Where to install it on accounts and repositories.

GitHubAppInfo.title: GitHubAppInfo
GitHubAppInfo.description: A GitHub App GitHub created from Kantel's manifest.

clientId.description: The OAuth client record made, once created.

GitHubAppSetup.title: GitHubAppSetup
GitHubAppSetup.description: A GitHub App manifest flow; GitHub requires it finished within an hour.

latestVersion.description: The newest version the control plane offers.

Host.title: Host
Host.description: A machine that runs sandboxes. It dials out to the control plane; it takes no inbound ports.

token.description: `kth_…`, shown once. It joins one host.

command.description: The one-line command that installs and registers a host with it.

HostState.description: `online`: connected and taking sandboxes. `unreachable`: its connection dropped; its sandboxes can't be reached until it is back. `draining`: connected, but takes no new sandboxes. `revoked`: its credential is revoked.

files.description: Every file of the package, `SKILL.md` among them.

extensions.description: Namespaced host data Kantel keeps but doesn't read, such as Lleverage's `lleverage.workflows`.

code.description: The join code, such as `kji_…`. Shown once, when the invite is made.

secret.description: The key itself, `ksk_…`. Shown once: store it now.

KeyInjection.title: KeyInjection
KeyInjection.description: How a key goes out on a request.

McpDiscovery.title: McpDiscovery
McpDiscovery.description: What Kantel learnt about a remote MCP server from its URL.

MemberRole.title: MemberRole
MemberRole.description: `member`: uses the organisation's shared sandboxes and snapshots and makes their own. `admin`: also manages members, API keys, webhooks, telemetry and the proxy. `owner`: also renames or deletes the organisation. A personal account's person is its `owner`.

includeInactive.description: Also list superseded and forgotten concepts, scoring a quarter.

snippet.description: The first statement line holding a term, cut to 160 characters.

MemorySnapshot.title: MemorySnapshot
MemorySnapshot.description: A whole space's concepts at one ref of a source.

MemorySnapshotRef.title: MemorySnapshotRef
MemorySnapshotRef.description: Where a space's snapshot came from, and when it was imported.

text.description: The message's words. May be empty when `attachments` has a file; otherwise it is `invalid`.

attachments.description: Files for this message, in the order they were attached. A deployment that stores no uploads refuses them (`invalid`), as it does a file from another project.

model.description: A model ID the session may use, for this run and the session's later runs. Absent keeps the session's model. Only a session's first message may choose its model: once the session has started, naming another is a `conflict` (naming its own is fine).

MessageBody.title: MessageBody
MessageBody.description: A message to the session's agent. `via` defaults to `prompt`.

MessageVia.title: MessageVia
MessageVia.description: How a message reaches the agent: `prompt` starts a run (queued behind one in progress), `steer` reaches a run in progress at its next model call, without stopping it (usually right after the tool call in progress), and `followUp` runs after the current run ends. A steer or follow-up to a session with no run in progress starts one, as a prompt does, so a message sent just as a run ends is never lost.

id.description: What a message's `model` names: a route such as `default`, or `<route>:<modelId>` for an override.

label.description: What a person reads, such as `Claude Sonnet 4.5`.

provider.description: Who serves the model, for grouping, such as `Anthropic`.

capabilities.description: What the model takes. A field left out is unknown.

default.description: The model the session runs with when no message names one. At most one.

disabledReason.description: Set when the model is listed but can't be chosen now, with the reason.

ModelOption.title: ModelOption
ModelOption.description: A model a session may run with, as a model picker shows it.

ModelProvider.title: ModelProvider
ModelProvider.description: The upstream: CLIProxyAPI, a LiteLLM proxy, Cloudflare AI Gateway or OpenRouter. Each speaks OpenAI's API and lists its models.

id.description: The connection's ID, which is its model connector's, such as `openrouter`.

vaultItemId.description: The vault item that holds the key. Never the key.

ModelProviderConnection.title: ModelProviderConnection
ModelProviderConnection.description: A saved connection: never its key.

baseUrl.description: For CLI Proxy API and LiteLLM: the OpenAI-compatible base URL, such as `http://host.docker.internal:4000/v1`. `http` or `https`, with no credentials. OpenRouter's is fixed; Cloudflare's is built from the IDs.

accountId.description: For Cloudflare AI Gateway: the Cloudflare account ID.

gatewayId.description: For Cloudflare AI Gateway: the gateway's ID. Default `default`.

ModelProviderInput.title: ModelProviderInput

issuer.description: An authorisation server's issuer, for a server with no template.

connections.description: How many connections are pinned to it.

public.description: A public client: no secret, so it signs in with a code or PKCE alone.

OAuthClient.title: OAuthClient
OAuthClient.description: An OAuth app registration at a tenancy level. Its secret is write-only.

OAuthClientTier.title: OAuthClientTier
OAuthClientTier.description: The tenancy level an OAuth client belongs to; `platform` is the deployment.

coalesced.description: How many due times this run stands for (more than 1 after missed runs).

result.description: How the run went: a task's `{ sessionId, submissionId }` (the session it started), a check's `{ exitCode, raised }`, or `{ error }` for a failed run.

OwnerRef.title: OwnerRef

PendingRun.title: PendingRun
PendingRun.description: The run is still going (or queued): ask again.

workspaceId.description: The session's workspace the file is in.

PresentedFile.description: A file the agent presented to the person (`present_files`). Read its bytes through the workspace read API with your own credentials.

organisationId.description: The organisation the project is in: always the caller's.

PromptAttachment.title: PromptAttachment
PromptAttachment.description: A file for a message, uploaded first: on Cloudflare `POST /v1/attachments?projectId=&name=` with the file's bytes as the body answers this reference. The message carries only the reference; the model sees the file's contents.

revocationUrl.description: Where a disconnect revokes the connection's tokens: RFC 7009, or the provider's own endpoint for `revocationStyle`. `{client_id}` is the connection's client ID.

deviceAuthorizationUrl.description: The device authorisation endpoint (RFC 8628). With a public client a connect signs in with a code typed at the provider.

icon.description: An https URL or a `data:image/svg+xml` URI.

apiHosts.description: Hosts the credential may be sent to. Never empty.

defaultHeaders.description: Headers every request through a connection made from it carries unless the agent sets its own, such as GitHub's `user-agent`. Never a credential.

manageAccessUrl.description: The provider's own page where a person removes an app's access.

attribution.description: Tell the upstream which sandbox and account each request came from, in signed `Kantel-Sandbox` and `Kantel-Account` headers.

RedactedConnectionUse.description: A use in a private session the caller can't open (#335): when, how it ended and for whom. No session, step, agent, project, request or reason.

twoPersonRule.description: Whoever publishes an edit may not be one of its authors.

kind.description: Kantel's `skills.skill`, `memory.space`, `workspace`, `models.connector` or `vault.item` (a secret in the encrypted store behind connections, under its stored name), or a kind a host registered, such as `workflows.workflow`.

ResourceRef.description: A resource: its kind and ID.

revision.description: Pins this revision. Without one, the share follows the latest.

ResourceSelector.description: A resource, optionally at one revision.

agentWrites.description: Whether agents covered by the share may write through it (`edit`, never `approve`). Off unless the granter turned it on.

parentShareId.description: The share a supervisor passed this one on from; revoking that revokes this.

RevocationOutcome.title: RevocationOutcome
RevocationOutcome.description: What a disconnect did at the provider: `revoked`, `unsupported` (the provider gives Kantel no way to revoke, or it is a key), `failed` (the provider refused or didn't answer; the connection is removed all the same) or `none` (nothing to revoke).

RevocationStyle.title: RevocationStyle
RevocationStyle.description: How a provider's revocation endpoint is called: `rfc7009` (a form POST of the token), or `github_grant` (GitHub's `DELETE /applications/{client_id}/grant`).

host.description: An exact host name, lower case.

command.description: A shell command line, run with `bash -lc` (or the isolate's shell).

detached.description: Start it and answer at once, with no time limit; read it back by its ID.

submissionId.description: The submission the message was answered as (`Submission.id`).

status.description: `answered`: the run reached its final answer; `failed`: a model or tool error ended it (`error` says which); `aborted`: someone aborted the session's run. Files it changed stay changed.

answer.description: The final answer's text, when it was answered.

RunResult.title: RunResult
RunResult.description: How the run a message started or joined ended.

subdomain.description: Its name under the deployment's sandbox domain, which its public port URLs start with.

image.description: The base image a microVM was made from, such as `ubuntu-24.04`.

reason.description: Why it is in `error` or `degraded`, in words.

autoStopMinutes.description: How long after a start or resume it stops by itself; `null` never.

stopsAt.description: When it will stop by itself, while running; the console's stops-in.

latestSnapshotId.description: The snapshot a resume or fork would use.

hostId.description: The host it runs on; only a super-admin is shown it.

pause.description: Whether it can be paused with its memory kept.

SandboxCapabilities.title: SandboxCapabilities
SandboxCapabilities.description: What this sandbox can do, from its type and its host.

SandboxHealth.title: SandboxHealth
SandboxHealth.description: `degraded`: the machine is up but its host can't fully reach it; it keeps running.

SandboxSizeName.title: SandboxSizeName
SandboxSizeName.description: A microVM's size; a deployment may offer fewer. Isolates have none.

sandboxId.description: Set when it was forked from another sandbox.

SandboxState.title: SandboxState
SandboxState.description: `starting`: being placed and booted. `running`: commands run now. `stopping`: its disk is being saved. `stopped`: no machine; its disk is kept as its newest snapshot, and running programs are gone. `paused`: like `stopped`, but its memory is kept too, so `resume` carries on where it left off (microVMs only). `error`: the last operation failed or the machine was lost; `recover` or `resume` it. `deleting`, `deleted`: erased for good, with its snapshots.

SandboxType.title: SandboxType
SandboxType.description: `isolate`: a workerd isolate with a JavaScript shell over the sandbox's files. Starts in milliseconds and costs almost nothing, but runs no native binaries, has no desktop and no SSH. `microvm`: a Firecracker microVM with a full Linux, root, Docker and `/dev/kvm` inside, a desktop, a browser and SSH.

SandboxVisibility.title: SandboxVisibility
SandboxVisibility.description: `private`: only the person who made it (and API keys of theirs) may see or use it. `organisation`: every member of its organisation may. A personal account's sandboxes are always `private`.

sandboxId.description: The sandbox to save, running or stopped.

snapshotId.description: Save this snapshot of the sandbox's history. Default: its state now.

replace.description: Replace a saved snapshot of the same name.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as `Europe/London`.

at.description: A one-off at this instant (epoch milliseconds). Exactly one of `at` and `repeat`.

until.description: No occurrence is due after this (epoch milliseconds).

nextDueAt.description: The next due time; absent when ended or paused.

occurrences.description: Occurrences so far; a coalesced one counts once.

ScheduleKind.title: ScheduleKind
ScheduleKind.description: What runs. A `task` starts a session with its payload `{ "agentId"?, "prompt" }` and sends the prompt exactly as written; a `check` runs its payload (a command line or an argument list) with no model.

dueAt.description: The next due times, soonest first.

ScopeSet.title: ScopeSet
ScopeSet.description: A named group of scopes, marked read or write.

resumed.description: True when deltas after the client's cursor follow, false for a snapshot.

ServerFrame.title: ServerFrame
ServerFrame.description: One frame of `@kantel/protocol`: `hello`, then a `snapshot` (or the deltas after the client's cursor), then live `delta`s.

SessionAudience.title: SessionAudience
SessionAudience.description: Who could see a session: only the person it acts for (`private`), or more people (`shared`).

ownerId.description: The owner's user or project ID; absent for the organisation's.

reason.description: Why the session may not use it.

viaShare.description: Usable because its owner shared it with the project.

SessionConnectionEligibility.title: SessionConnectionEligibility
SessionConnectionEligibility.description: Whether a session may use one connection, and if not, why (#335).

nextCursor.description: Present when older items exist; pass it as `cursor`.

locked.description: Set once the session has started (it holds a message): its model is `selected`'s for good, and a message naming another is a `conflict`. Its thinking level can still change.

SessionModelState.title: SessionModelState
SessionModelState.description: The models a session's messages may name (`model` and `thinking` on a message), in the order to show them; `selected`, what the session's next model call uses (its agent profile's until its first message names another); `defaults`, what its agent profile names; and `locked`, set once the session has started. The first message fixes the session's model, so everything in its transcript comes from one model; its thinking level can change on any later message, though a change may cost the next call the provider's prompt cache.

projectId.description: The session's project. Absent for a session scoped to the organisation.

agentId.description: The agent profile the session runs.

userId.description: The person the session works for: whose own skills and prompt rules it gets.

pinnedAt.description: When the session was pinned to the top of the list, in epoch milliseconds.

archivedAt.description: When the session was archived (out of the default list), in epoch milliseconds.

markedUnreadAt.description: When someone marked the session unread, in epoch milliseconds.

SessionScope.title: SessionScope
SessionScope.description: Where a session works: `project` (in `projectId`) or `organisation`, above every project and in none of them.

items.description: The latest page of items, oldest first.

SessionUnattended.title: SessionUnattended
SessionUnattended.description: Started by a schedule, with no person watching: the schedule and occurrence it runs for (#335). With `userId`, a scheduled run acting for the person who made the schedule (a one-person deployment): it may use their own connections while it is private to them, and the organisation's and projects' only when they allow unattended use. Only a host app or Kantel names one; a child session has its parent's.

SessionVisibility.title: SessionVisibility
SessionVisibility.description: Who may see the session (#335). `private`: only the person it acts for (and the host app that made it); no project or organisation member, an admin included. `shared` (the default): its project's members, or the organisation's. A person's private connection is refused in a shared session unless they shared it with the project.

container.description: The session's container: `started` now, already `running`, `skipped` (the session has never needed one, so none is started for it) or `unavailable` (this deployment runs no containers, or the session has no workspace).

modelId.description: One of the models it lists. No `:`, which names a thinking level.

redirectUri.description: This deployment's redirect URI, to register exactly.

SetupGuide.description: How to register an app for a template, with this deployment's values in it.

SetupStep.description: One step of registering an app at a provider.

SetupTier.title: SetupTier
SetupTier.description: How a template connects for the caller: `none` (nothing to set up), `public_client` (the deployment's client with no secret), `own_app` (an app the person or project registers), `host_client` (the deployment's or the organisation's client) or `key`.

ShareAccess.title: ShareAccess
ShareAccess.description: `restricted`: only those who can see the session's workspace. `link`: anyone with the link.

ShareGrantee.description: Who a share is for: a project (its sessions, and its people within their role), an agent profile, a person, or one session (what a supervisor passes on).

ShareUse.description: A resource a session used through a share: which revision, under which share.

SnapshotConcept.description: One concept as a host's source holds it.

ToolServerTransport.title: ToolServerTransport
ToolServerTransport.description: How Kantel reaches the server: `tunnel`, the server's side dials out over a WebSocket; `http`, Streamable HTTP to a public URL; `callback`, signed HTTPS host callbacks. Only `tunnel` is built yet.

draining.description: Stop placing new sandboxes on it.

extendMinutes.description: Move `stopsAt` to this long from now.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as `Europe/London`.

at.description: A one-off at this instant (epoch milliseconds), or `null` to clear it, as when it becomes a recurrence. Exactly one of `at` and `repeat` is left set.

repeat.description: The recurrence, or `null` to clear it, as when it becomes a one-off.

until.description: No occurrence is due after this (epoch milliseconds), or `null` to drop the end date.

count.description: At most this many occurrences, or `null` to drop the run limit.

UpdateScheduleBody.title: UpdateScheduleBody
UpdateScheduleBody.description: The fields to change; a field left out stays as it is, and `null` on `at`, `repeat`, `until` or `count` clears it. The owner and the kind are fixed at create.

UpdateShareBody.title: UpdateShareBody
UpdateShareBody.description: The fields to change; one left out stays as it is.

placeholder.description: The connection's placeholder (#331), sent in the credential's place.

env.description: The sandbox's environment variable holding it, such as KANTEL_CONNECTION_GITHUB.

UsableConnection.title: UsableConnection
UsableConnection.description: A connection as a session sees it: no credential.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description: Model token usage and cost: the session's running total on a snapshot and in a `usage` op, the answer's on a run result. `inputTokens` excludes input read from or written to the provider's cache.

recentCpu.description: CPU utilisation, 0 to 1, over the last 24 intervals of 5 minutes, oldest first: a sparkline.

UserAttachment.title: UserAttachment
UserAttachment.description: A file sent with a message. The model saw its contents; `text` leaves them out.

callId.description: The tool call waiting on this approval: a connection call's `callId`, or for a request a `codemode` script made, the script's inner call (`<scriptCallId>/<key>`, such as `toolu_01/c9`). A client that renders that call may show the approval in it and leave this card out; one that doesn't still has the card. Absent on cards written before it.

VaultApprovalCard.title: VaultApprovalCard
VaultApprovalCard.description: A `ConnectionApprovalCard` under its old type, `vault.approval`, as transcripts written before the rename carry it. Deprecated: a reader takes both types for one release.

viewOnly.description: Watch only: no keyboard or mouse. Default false.

Webhook.title: Webhook
Webhook.description: An HTTPS endpoint that gets an account's events, signed as Standard Webhooks are: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body`, keyed by the secret after its `whsec_`). Failed deliveries are retried with backoff, up to 8 attempts.
